settings.title: Settings

skills.title: Skills
skills.desc: Capabilities the Custom AI can use. Disabling a skill removes its tools and its prompt guidance from the next conversation.
skills.toolCount: {n, plural, one {# API tool} other {# API tools}}
skills.empty: No skills available (the skill manifest could not be loaded).
skills.calendarChatNote: This toggle only governs the outward Skill interface and capability declaration; the calendar tools in chat are controlled by the Calendar item under System capabilities.
skills.notionAgentMasterOff: Master switch MAILAGENT_NOTION_AGENT_TOOL is off: even when enabled here, the notion_agent tool won't be registered in chat.
skills.skillCreatorChatNote: This Skill provides workflow guidance; approval profiles for its 6 chat tools are under Connectors & Tools → Skill supply chain.
skills.customAgentChatNote: This Skill provides workflow guidance; approval profiles for its 7 chat tools are under Connectors & Tools → Custom Agent.
skills.argvPattern: Argv pattern (one item per line; prefix regex with pattern:)

skillDrafts.title: Skill drafts
skillDrafts.desc: Isolated drafts are never executable. Review validation and publish explicitly.
skillDrafts.mcpDetected: Detected MCP Servers: {names}. This version does not import them yet.

connectors.title: External connections (MCP)
connectors.desc: Connect external services such as Notion or Jira over the MCP protocol. Once connected you decide tool by tool what the AI may call.
connectors.loadError: Could not load the connection list: {message}
connectors.connectWeb: The remote web app cannot start a connection (the authorization callback goes to a local address) — use the desktop app.
connectors.authTimeout: Authorization timed out: no browser callback within {seconds} seconds. Please try again.
connectors.enabledHelper: When off, none of this service's tools are given to the AI; credentials and per-tool settings are kept.
connectors.preprocess: Allow email pre-processing to call it
connectors.preprocessHelper: Lets the email pre-processing classifier call this service. That venue runs unattended: only tools whose tier is “Auto” are available (“Needs approval” behaves as unavailable there); write tools set to “Auto” are exposed to it too.

custom.desc: Connect a custom Streamable HTTP / SSE MCP endpoint or a local lazy-started stdio MCP process (headers and env secrets are encrypted at rest; desktop only).
custom.urlHint: Remote endpoints must use https://; http:// is allowed for localhost / 127.0.0.1.
custom.syncWarning: Saved connection, but tool sync failed
custom.idInvalid: ID must be 2–48 lowercase letters, digits, underscores, or hyphens starting with alphanumeric
custom.commandRequired: Command is required for stdio connectors
custom.deleteDesc: Stops any running local process for this connector and removes its encrypted secrets and tool manifest.

disconnectDialog.title: Disconnect {name}?
disconnectDialog.desc: This deletes the credentials stored on this machine, and the service's tools stop being available to the AI immediately. The tool list and per-tool permissions are kept and apply again after reconnecting.
disconnectDialog.purgeHelper: Removes the connection row and its tool list as well (as if it had never been added). Unticked, only the credentials are deleted and the per-tool tiers survive a reconnect.

tools.loadError: Could not load the tool list: {message}
tools.empty: No tools synced yet — use “Sync tools” above to fetch the list.
tools.defaultHint: Default tier: read runs Auto; write, update, and destructive tools require Approval.
tools.orphanTip: The remote server no longer offers this tool; the setting is kept but the tool is not given to the AI.

effective.ask: Currently: asks for approval on every call

toolfaceNotice.title: Tool surface widened under the new default
toolfaceNotice.body: This connection offers {reads} read and {writes} write/update tools ({destructive} marked destructive). The default tier is “Auto” (runs without an approval card) — expand the list below to adjust tools one by one.

destructiveAutoDialog.title: Set a destructive tool to “Auto”?
destructiveAutoDialog.desc: The service marks {name} as destructive (it may overwrite or delete existing data). On “Auto”, the AI will call it without asking you first.
destructiveAutoDialog.bulkDesc: This group contains {count} tools the service marks as destructive. On “Auto”, the AI will call them without asking you first.

managed.uninstallDialogDesc: This stops the local runtime, deletes its managed files from disk, and clears the saved connection configuration.
managed.runtimeMissing: Local runtime binary is missing — click “Install & enable” to repair it.
managed.platformUnsupported: This local runtime does not support the current operating system or CPU architecture.
managed.webDisabled: Managed local runtimes install and control apps on this computer — manage them inside the desktop app.
managed.pixelPrivacyBody: privacyMaskMiddleware only redacts outbound text tool parameters and outputs — it does not blur or mask pixels inside web or desktop screenshots. Raw image frames are sent directly to your configured vision-capable LLM.
managed.browserModeHelper: Choose how Browser Use attaches to a browser. Switching modes restarts the local MCP process on next call.

cdp_chrome.title: Attach to running Chrome (CDP)
cdp_chrome.desc: Connects via Chrome Remote Debugging so existing logins and extensions stay available inside your everyday browser.

extension.title: Playwright MCP Extension
extension.desc: Bridges through the Playwright MCP browser extension without launching Chrome with a debugging flag.

isolated_profile.title: Built-in persistent managed browser (Headless)
isolated_profile.desc: MailAgent-managed persistent browser profile that runs silently with zero Chrome debug prompts and supports one-click Chrome cookie import or manual sign-in window.

managed.cdpGuideBody: Open the address below in Chrome and enable the remote debugging toggle so Browser Use can attach to your tabs:
managed.tccSubtitle: Desktop Use needs Accessibility control and Screen Recording permission granted to the desktop app.
managed.tccWebDisabled: System permission checks are only available inside the desktop app.
managed.tccAccessibilityDesc: Required to inspect UI elements and perform mouse clicks or keystrokes.
managed.tccScreenRecordingDesc: Required to capture desktop and window screenshots for visual grounding.
managed.headlessDesc: Hides the browser window by default so automation never steals focus; turn this off or launch the dedicated window when visual inspection is needed.
managed.headlessEnabledToast: Headless mode enabled (takes effect on next run)
managed.headlessDisabledToast: Headless mode disabled; browser window will be visible on next run
managed.importChromeDesc: Decrypts and copies cookies from your local Chrome profile into the built-in managed browser without affecting Chrome; open the dedicated window once for SSO/LocalStorage apps.
managed.importChromeDone: Imported {count} cookies from {profile} into built-in browser
managed.launchWindowDone: Managed browser window opened; sign-ins here persist automatically
managed.launchWindowFailed: Failed to open managed browser window
managed.launchWindowHint: Tip: Cookie-based logins can use one-click import; both imported cookies and manual window logins persist in the managed profile.

connectors.supersededHint: This connection is a self-hosted direct link, but the service now ships through Composio. Use “Switch track” to disconnect and clear its config, then reconnect from the catalog.

selfHosted.serverUrlHint: Point to the deployed Streamable HTTP `/mcp` endpoint (e.g. https://canvas.chenge.ink/mcp).
selfHosted.tokenHint: Encrypted in your local keychain; leave blank only for unauthenticated local dev servers.
selfHosted.webDisabled: Self-hosted preset setup is only available from the desktop app.

catalog.title: Preset catalog
catalog.outboundNotice: Preset connections execute through the Composio cloud: tool inputs and results pass through their servers and the OAuth tokens are held on their side. For services you want to reach directly, use “custom MCP” (a later release).
catalog.supersedes: The old direct configuration of the same service is still listed above — disconnect and clear it first.
catalog.gateTitle: Add a Composio API key to use the preset catalog
catalog.gateBody:
1. Create an account at app.composio.dev (the free tier includes 20K tool calls/month — plenty for personal use)
2. Generate a key under Settings → API Keys
3. Paste it into the field above and save
Once saved, every service in the catalog is one click away.

outboundDialog.title: Preset connections send data to Composio

desc.artifact_server: Artifact Server: publish interactive HTML dashboards, decks, and prototypes to your own Cloudflare/self-hosted workspace for versioned sharing and review comments.
desc.asana: Asana: search tasks and projects, create tasks and comments, update tasks.
desc.browser_use: Browser Use: control Chrome or an isolated browser via Playwright MCP — inspect tabs, fill forms, capture screenshots.
desc.desktop_use: Desktop Use: operate desktop apps via Agent Desktop MCP — accessibility tree, click, type, and screen capture.
desc.figma: Figma: read file structure and components, pull design variables, render nodes, comment.
desc.github: GitHub: read repo content and READMEs, browse issues/PRs, open issues and comments.
desc.gmail: Gmail: search and read mail and drafts, read contacts; drafting only — no sending.
desc.googlecalendar: Google Calendar: read events and free slots, create/update/delete events.
desc.googledrive: Google Drive: find files, read metadata and comments, create folders and text files.
desc.intercom: Intercom: read conversations/contacts/tickets, search support records and articles.
desc.linear: Linear: browse issues and projects, create issues and comments, update state.
desc.notion: Notion: search and read pages/databases, create pages, append content, comment.
desc.outlook: Outlook: calendar and contacts (🔴 no mail send/draft — the local Exchange chain stays the only write path).
desc.paypal: PayPal: read-only invoices, payments, orders, subscriptions and disputes.
desc.sentry: Sentry: read projects and error issues, event details, alerts and stats.
desc.slack: Slack: read channels and history, search messages, post messages and reactions.
desc.stripe: Stripe: read-only finance data (customers, charges, invoices, subscriptions, disputes).
desc.twitter: X (Twitter): search posts, read timelines and analytics, post and bookmark.

imFeishu.title: Feishu chat
imFeishu.desc: Talk to this machine's AI assistant from a Feishu direct message (same memory, same persona). This is where you can see whether it is connected, who it is bound to, which tools it may use there, and what has been approved.
imFeishu.disabledHint: Not enabled: set MAILAGENT_IM_FEISHU=true in .env, then restart the backend and the app.
imFeishu.noCredential: No app credentials for the chat bot yet — fill in the App ID and App Secret under "App credentials" below and save.
imFeishu.conflict: Another MailAgent instance was detected ({reason}). Feishu does not broadcast to multiple long-lived connections, so instances would steal each other's messages — this one deliberately did not connect. Keep only one running (stop the pm2 mail-sync process when using the desktop app).

credential.title: App credentials
credential.present: Configured: App ID {appId} · last updated {time}. The App Secret is never shown again — paste a new one to rotate it.
credential.absent: Not configured yet. Create a separate custom app in the Feishu open platform (do not reuse the notification bot), then enter its App ID and App Secret below.
credential.restartHint: Restart the backend ("Restart now" in the banner above) before the new credentials are used: if none were configured before, the worker has not started at all, and a live connection is never hot-swapped.
credential.platformHint: You still need to finish the app setup in the Feishu open platform: enable the bot capability, request the direct-message permission, and pick long-lived connection in BOTH the "Event subscription" and "Callback subscription" tabs. See docs/reference/llm-agent/im-feishu-chat.md.
credential.envSeedHint: You can also put FEISHU_IM_APP_ID / FEISHU_IM_APP_SECRET in {path} to seed them at first start — but those keys are only a default for "nothing stored yet"; once credentials exist, changing them has no effect.
credential.unbound: A different Feishu app was detected, so the previously bound account was released (open_id is issued per app, so the old one is meaningless under the new app). Generate a new pairing code after restarting the backend.
credential.webDisabled: Credentials cannot be written from the remote web app (this swaps the identity of this machine's execution channel) — use the desktop app.

bind.title: Bound Feishu account
bind.sameNameTrap: Two Feishu apps can share a display name — identify by app_id / open_id, never by name.
bind.unbound: Not bound yet. Only the bound Feishu account reaches the command channel; everyone else is refused.
bind.codePending: A pairing code is already waiting (valid until {time}). Generate a new one if you lost it.
bind.webDisabled: Pairing cannot be started from the remote web app — it wires a Feishu account into this machine's execution channel. Do it in the desktop app.
bind.flagOffDisabled: Feishu chat is not enabled, so no bot could receive a code right now.
bind.failed: Could not generate a pairing code

pair.howto: Open a direct message with the bot in Feishu and send it those 6 digits on their own.

tools.title: Tools the AI may use in Feishu
tools.desc: Feishu is a deliberately narrowed venue (a stolen Feishu account is not a stolen computer). These are fixed rules, not settings.
tools.read: Reads (mail / calendar / search / reports / conversation lookup): run without approval.
tools.write: Writes (send, save draft, flag, reschedule…): every call needs a tap on the Feishu approval card; no auto-approve list applies.
tools.connector: External service (MCP) tools: all available; reads run freely, writes always need approval (destructive tools carry a red warning on the card).
tools.web: Web access (search / fetch): controlled by the switch below, off by default; even when on, every call needs approval.
tools.denied: Local commands, file read/write, config and skill changes, and calls out to third-party AI are not registered in Feishu at all — the model cannot see them. Use the desktop app or the remote web app for those.

web.title: Allow web access in Feishu chats
web.desc: Lets the AI search and fetch web pages from Feishu. Off by default: web content is untrusted, and a stolen Feishu account is not a stolen computer. Each call still needs approval.
web.restartHint: Takes effect after restarting the app (the AI engine reads this once at startup).
web.webDisabled: This switch cannot be changed from the remote web app — use the desktop app.

approvals.title: Approvals in Feishu conversations
approvals.desc: The last 10 approve / reject decisions a human actually made. The criterion is "this conversation came from Feishu" — if such a conversation was approved from the desktop app instead, it is still listed here (the record cannot tell which side was tapped). Calls that skipped the card are not counted.
approvals.unavailable: Approval history is unreadable right now (the chat database is not accessible) — this does not mean nothing was ever approved.
approvals.empty: Nothing has been approved or rejected in a Feishu conversation yet.

systemCapabilities.title: System capabilities
systemCapabilities.desc: Every capability family the assistant can call in chat. Toggleable ones use a real switch (web access); the rest are env-controlled and read-only here: enabled shows a locked state, and disabled ones are still shown (disabled state).
systemCapabilities.lockedTip: This capability is toggled by an environment variable and cannot be switched here at runtime.
systemCapabilities.disabledTip: This capability is currently disabled via an environment variable; edit .env and restart the backend to enable it.

coreEmail.title: Core email actions
coreEmail.desc: Lets the assistant draft replies, compose/forward drafts, edit drafts, flag, archive, pin, resync, and send email (write tools + send).
coreEmail.control: Core capability · always available; every write executes only after an approval card.

kos.title: KOS knowledge brain
kos.desc: Lets the assistant search and read the Gbrain cross-domain knowledge graph: semantic retrieval, keyword full-text, read a whole page, find domain experts, list pages by type/tag, and see what links to a page.
kos.control: Core read · always registered; retrieval depends on whether Gbrain is configured.

selfMount.title: Self-config meta tools
selfMount.desc: Lets the assistant view/update its own identity docs and discover/mount skills (update_system_md / discover_skills / set_skill_enabled).

calendar.title: Calendar tools (chat)
calendar.desc: Lets the assistant read/write the calendar in chat (list / get / reschedule / RSVP / delete); unrelated to the calendar skill toggle in the Skills list (which only governs the outward Skill interface).

session.title: Session retrieval
session.desc: Lets the assistant search your past AI conversation history (list / search / read).

config.title: Agent self-config
config.desc: Lets the assistant view and adjust its own identity docs and memory (read / history / restore / update memory).

web.title: Web access
web.desc: Lets the assistant fetch web pages and run web searches (web fetch + web search).
web.restartHint: Quit and reopen the App for changes to take effect.

tavily.label: Tavily API Key
tavily.helper: web_search defaults to DuckDuckGo, which is blocked on mainland-China networks; enter a Tavily API key to switch to Tavily (reachable in China). Separate multiple Tavily keys with commas to auto-rotate when one runs out of quota; leave empty to use DuckDuckGo (unreachable in China). Stored only in the local .env, never returned to the UI. Takes effect on save.

exec.title: Command / file access
exec.desc: Manage the no-approval allowlist for the assistant running commands and reading/writing files.

skillPacks.title: Skill packs
skillPacks.desc: Install, configure, and uninstall third-party skill packs.

customAgents.title: Custom Agents
customAgents.desc: Create automated agents triggered on a schedule or by email.

memory.title: Memory
memory.desc: Durable facts the Custom AI remembers about you. Edits and deletions take effect on the next conversation.
memory.empty: No memory yet. The agent saves facts here as you confirm them.

imageGenModel.title: Image Generation Model
imageGenModel.desc: The model the generate_image tool uses to create or edit images in chat. Only OpenAI or OpenAI-compatible providers can be selected (the AI SDK implements the image endpoints for those two protocols only). Takes effect on save, no restart needed.
imageGenModel.label: Image model
imageGenModel.helper: Candidates = enabled models of the enabled OpenAI / OpenAI-compatible providers under Model Services. Leave empty and an image request in chat will point you back here.
imageGenModel.noCandidates: No candidate models: add and enable an OpenAI or OpenAI-compatible provider under Model Services first, then enable its image model (e.g. gpt-image-1).

memoryCaptureModel.title: Memory Extraction Model
memoryCaptureModel.desc: The model used when auto memory (memory.md) extracts durable facts from your conversations. Only takes effect when memory auto-capture is enabled.
memoryCaptureModel.label: Extraction model
memoryCaptureModel.helper: This model runs once per captured conversation turn — pick a fast, cheap small model (e.g. claude-haiku-4-5). Leave empty to use the haiku default. Requires a backend restart to take effect.

userMdCompile.title: Compile Preferences from Memory
userMdCompile.desc: Merge AI-captured preference memories into user.md. Takes effect immediately after triggering manually.
userMdCompile.noChange: No new preferences found to compile

standingDocs.title: Identity & Memory Docs
standingDocs.desc: View and manually edit the 4 Standing Context identity documents (SOUL / AGENT / RULES / USER) plus the auto-maintained memory (memory.md). Changes take effect on the next conversation.
standingDocs.floorNote: PRODUCT_SAFETY_FLOOR is always prepended at the code layer — document content cannot weaken it. Override phrasing in RULES is rejected server-side.
standingDocs.memoryNote: memory.md is auto-extracted and rewritten by the AI from your conversations, and you can also edit it manually. It is injected into every conversation as BACKGROUND memory (not an identity doc) and cannot weaken the safety floor.
standingDocs.overBudgetHint: Content exceeds the {budget}-character budget; trim it before saving.

execPolicy.title: Automation policy
execPolicy.helper: The assistant needs your approval every time it runs a command or reads/writes files. This is the allowlist you built via “Always allow” for exact operations: matching operations run without approval, everything else still prompts. To loosen a rule, delete and recreate it (in-place editing is not supported, to avoid silently widening scope).
execPolicy.empty: No automation policies yet. When the assistant asks to run a command or read/write files, tick “Always allow” to create an allowlist entry for that exact operation — matching operations then run without approval.

providers.title: Model services
providers.helper: Manage LLM upstream providers: official APIs, OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible relays, and local engines can coexist. The default provider carries over the legacy gateway config.
providers.empty: No providers yet. Click “Add” in the corner to create one from a template.
providers.catalogUpToDate: Model catalog is already up to date
providers.catalogSyncFailed: Catalog refresh failed; keeping cached catalog

apiKey.label: API key
apiKey.set: Set (····{last4}) — enter a new value and save to rotate

keyPool.title: Backup key pool (429 rotation)
keyPool.helper: Enter one spare API key per line. Automatically rotates past HTTP 429 cooldowns while staying sticky on the primary key when healthy.
keyPool.placeholder:
One spare key per line, e.g.
sk-spare-1
sk-spare-2

headers.label: Custom headers
headers.opencodeSessionHint: OpenCode requires an x-opencode-session header. MailAgent attaches a random ID per conversation automatically (used only for OpenCode routing and caching; it contains no conversation content), so there is no need to add it here. If you add one, your value is used instead.
headers.incrementalHint: Supports per-header updates and deletions without re-entering other stored secrets.
headers.setPlaceholder: Configured (enter a new value to replace)
headers.reenterHint: Header values are write-only — re-enter every kept value before saving

models.title: Models
models.empty: No models yet. Click “Fetch model list” to pull from upstream, or add one manually below (fallback for relays that don't expose /models).
models.noMatch: No models match the current filter.
models.manualPlaceholder: Add a model id manually (wire id)

add.desc: Pick a cloud or local template, verify connectivity, and save to fetch models.
add.baseUrlRequired: Required (this protocol has no official default endpoint)

privacyMask.label: Privacy masking
privacyMask.helper: Replace secrets, IDs, phones, emails, and custom regexes with placeholders locally before sending and restore them on arrival (fails closed with HTTP 503 on error).

privacyMask.title: Outbound Privacy Masking
privacyMask.helper: Per-provider bidirectional local redaction: replaces sensitive data with [[PII_TYPE_N]] before leaving this machine and restores original values locally. Only hit counts are stored.
privacyMask.loadFailed: Failed to load privacy masking config
privacyMask.saveFailed: Failed to save privacy masking rules

secret.label: API keys & tokens
secret.helper: Masks sk-, mak_, AIza, ghp_, and AKIA secret tokens

id_card.label: National ID (18-digit checksum)
id_card.helper: Validated with ISO 7064 check digit to avoid order-ID false positives

phone.label: Mobile phone numbers
phone.helper: Matches mainland mobile numbers including +86 prefix

email.label: Email addresses
email.helper: Masks emails outbound and restores them inside text and tool call inputs

bank_card.label: Bank card numbers (Luhn)
bank_card.helper: Matches 16–19 digit sequences verified by Luhn checksum

customRules.title: Custom regex rules
customRules.helper: Add custom regex patterns (e.g. EMP-\d{6}); syntax and catastrophic ReDoS patterns are checked before saving.

usageDashboard.title: AI Usage & Cache Monitor
usageDashboard.helper: Unified token spend, token-weighted prompt cache hit rate, estimated USD cost, and latest 50 connectivity/runtime probe logs across chat, agents, groups, reports, and email processing.
usageDashboard.shortcutHelper: Token spend, prompt cache hit rate trends, surface/model billing, and latest 50 probe/error logs now live in Operations → LLM Dashboard.
usageDashboard.shortcutCardHelper: Inspect live token spend, cache savings, and probe logs in the Operations view
usageDashboard.emptyRange: No LLM calls recorded in this window.

probelog.title: Probe & error diagnostics (latest 50)
probelog.empty: No diagnostic or probe logs yet.

skillPacks.title: Skill install
skillPacks.helper: Install third-party skill packs from GitHub repos (owner/repo or URL), npm packages (npm:@scope/pkg), archive URLs, or local paths. Two-phase: fetch a preview, review contents and declarations, then confirm.
skillPacks.installedCount: {count, plural, one {# skill pack installed.} other {# skill packs installed.}}

updates.upToDateToast: All installed skills are up to date

dialog.title: Install Skill
dialog.desc: Two-phase install: fetch a pack preview, manually review the file list, secret declarations and SKILL.md excerpt, then install once confirmed. Third-party content is unverified — review it carefully.
dialog.staleError: The pack contents changed after the preview, so the install was rejected. Fetch a new preview and review again.
dialog.remoteHelper: Supports GitHub (ChenyqThu/omada-ui-kit), npm (npm:@chenyqthu/omada-ui-kit), or .zip / .tgz archive URLs.
dialog.multipleSkillsPrompt: Multiple skills found in this repository. Choose one to install:
dialog.installedSecretsHint: This skill declares {count} secret(s) ({names}); set them under its “Config”.

config.title: config.json (non-sensitive config, plaintext, shared with the script)

secret.replacePlaceholder: Enter a new value to replace
secret.sectionDesc: Secrets are write-only: the value is never shown after saving, only the name and update time. Values are stored encrypted and injected as environment variables when the script runs.

pack.uninstallWarning: This will delete the skill's on-disk directory, its registration row, and clear all of its stored secrets. This cannot be undone.

settings.accentHint: 6 swatches · drives the primary CTA + chip color

page.intro: Accent, theme, language, glass material and the tab workspace. Preferences stay local.
page.title: General

accent.note: Drives the toolbar, selected row, status chips, Island accent and batch-bar badge. Each change broadcasts to the ping-island bridge.

language.title: Language
language.zhMeta: UI · toolbar · settings · AI quick actions. Email body is never auto-translated.
language.enMeta: UI · toolbar · settings · AI quick actions. Email body never auto-translated.
language.note: List headers (MAILBOXES · AI FIELDS · ATTACHMENTS) stay in English mono, unaffected by body font size or density.

theme.title: Theme
theme.systemMeta: Follows macOS appearance toggle — works out of the box.

surface.title: Surface
surface.frostedMeta: Frosted · one sheet of glass: OS-level blur + tint. Mood & tuning below.
surface.solidMeta: Solid · opaque, zero blur & glow. Best perf, matches prefers-reduced-transparency.

tabWorkspace.title: Tab workspace

limit.label: Tab limit
limit.meta: How many email / matter tabs can stay open at once

tabWorkspace.note: Opening one more past the limit closes the least recently viewed tab. Only an unsaved reply or draft keeps a tab from closing automatically; a tab you have chatted with in the AI drawer closes like any other — it just isn't reused when you move to the next or previous email. Lowering the limit does not close anything retroactively — it applies the next time you open a tab.

bodyText.title: Body text
bodyText.note: Font, size and line height apply to the email reading area; compose line height applies to the composer and is sent with the email, so recipients see the same spacing you typed. Defaults: 1.15 reading, 1.5 compose. List rows, AI fields and other UI text are unaffected.

composeLineHeight.label: Compose line height
composeLineHeight.meta: Spacing in the composer and in sent mail

mood.neutralMeta: Near-neutral and restrained — closest to the macOS system material. Reading first.
mood.tintedMeta: Accent mixed into the glass + one ambient light from the top-left. Strongest brand feel.
mood.brightMeta: Whitened base with lifted brightness — airy and light, close to acrylic.

knobs.title: Advanced glass tuning
knobs.blurNote: Blur is provided by the OS here; this slider only applies on platforms without native glass.
knobs.note: Switching mood resets tuning; Reset only clears the sliders, not the mood. Everything applies live and is stored locally.

export.label: Export diagnostics bundle
export.helper: Bundles the last 7 days of runtime logs plus a redacted config snapshot for troubleshooting. May take about a minute to generate.

attachToFeedback.label: Attach the diagnostics bundle when sending feedback
attachToFeedback.helper: Controls the default state of that checkbox in the feedback dialog. Same bundle as the export above.

settings.secretPlaceholder: Paste new value to save · current value not shown

env.remoteReadonly: Remote is read-only; edit settings on the host machine

search.placeholder: Search settings, env keys, or keywords…

page.title: Labs
page.intro: Manage experimental capabilities that are still under validation.

labs.warning: Experimental features may be unstable. Once promoted, they move into their regular settings area.

advanced.label: Advanced experiments
advanced.helper: Low-level capabilities for protocol compatibility and developer debugging.

groupAgents.label: Multi-agent group chat (experimental)
groupAgents.helper: Lets the local AI service drive who speaks in a group: each member's response mode decides who wakes up, members can reply to each other, and every round is bounded by the chain cap and hourly budgets. Turn it off to go back to "you send one message, each member replies once". Takes effect immediately — no restart.

skillCatalogPrompt.label: Skill catalog prompt
skillCatalogPrompt.helper: Inject the skill catalog into the AI system prompt for discoverability, adding about 300 tokens per turn.

memoryLayers.label: Five-layer memory organization
memoryLayers.helper: Automatically classifies extracted memories into identity, preferences, context, dynamics, and experience with isolated budgets per layer.

agUiMirror.label: AG-UI protocol mirror
agUiMirror.helper: Expose the developer-oriented AG-UI protocol mirror endpoint for compatibility testing and debugging.

notion.title: Notion integration

manual.title: Enter token and database IDs manually
manual.helper: For a self-built internal integration, or when you need to point at different databases.

connect.label: Connect Notion
connect.helper: Authorize once in your browser (you can duplicate the official template on the way). The token and both database IDs are written automatically — nothing to paste.

oauth.connectedHelper: Connected via Notion authorization. "Remove connection from this Mac" only clears local config; to revoke on Notion's side, go to Notion → Settings → My connections.
oauth.doneDetail: Connected. Email database "{emailDb}", calendar database "{calendarDb}". Restart the backend to start syncing to Notion.

folderSizeLimit.label: IMAP folder view limit (messages)

The cost: older messages outside the window are invisible at the IMAP layer (history already synced locally is unaffected; this only limits what incremental sync and write operations such as flag / archive can reach). Default 500; set 0 to leave this key entirely to DavMail.

Prerequisite: this depends on AI email preprocessing running, otherwise nothing ever gets labeled.

guide.toggle: How to get a public address
guide.intro: Cloud agents such as Notion can only reach a public HTTPS address, so a public address is required for them. Local clients such as Claude Code or Cursor can use the local address directly.
guide.recommend: We recommend a Cloudflare Zero Trust Tunnel to forward the local address to the internet.
guide.step1: In Cloudflare Zero Trust → Networks → Tunnels, create or pick a tunnel, then install and run cloudflared on this Mac.
guide.step2: Add a Public Hostname to the tunnel: any subdomain (e.g. mcp), Path ^/mcp$, Service http://localhost:{port}.
guide.step3: Do not create a Cloudflare Access application for this hostname, or requests will be sent to a login page.
guide.step4: Enter https://{host}/mcp as the public address above and click Check.
guide.agentTask:
Please expose the MailAgent MCP server on this Mac to the internet with a Cloudflare Tunnel.

Goal: expose http://localhost:{port}/mcp as https://{host}/mcp through a Cloudflare Tunnel.

Steps:
1. In Cloudflare Zero Trust → Networks → Tunnels, create or pick a tunnel, then install and run cloudflared on this Mac.
2. Add a Public Hostname to the tunnel: any subdomain (e.g. mcp), Path ^/mcp$, Service http://localhost:{port}.
3. Do not create a Cloudflare Access application for this hostname, or requests will be sent to a login page.
4. When done, tell me the final address https://{host}/mcp. I will enter it as the public address under MailAgent Settings → MCP Server and click Check.

Constraints:
- Only expose the /mcp path. Do not expose any other path of the local API.
- Do not put Cloudflare Access in front of this hostname.
- cloudflared must keep running; supervise it with launchd or pm2.

Acceptance:
- curl -i https://{host}/mcp should return 405 with the response header Allow: POST.
- A 302 redirect to cloudflareaccess.com means Access is blocking it; remove the Access application for this hostname.

create.title: New access key
create.desc: Name the key so you can tell which agent is using it.

editScopes.title: Edit permissions for “{label}”
editScopes.desc: Changes take effect immediately. The key itself stays the same, so configured clients do not need updating.

clientConfig.rowHelper: Creates a .bak backup and surgically merges the MailAgent MCP entry into your local client config.
clientConfig.dialogDesc: Updates only mcpServers.mailagent while preserving all other config keys and writing a .bak backup.
clientConfig.apiKeyHint: Leave blank to insert the <YOUR_MAILAGENT_API_KEY> placeholder for previewing or manual editing.

email_organize.label: Organize mail
email_organize.desc: Flag, pin and archive. Can be undone.

matters_write.label: Edit matters
matters_write.desc: Create matters, add notes, add and update action items.

calendar_write.label: Edit calendar
calendar_write.desc: Reply to invites, reschedule and delete events. Attendees are notified.

email_write.label: Send mail
email_write.desc: Sends real email and cannot be undone. Mail an external agent reads may carry injected instructions, so keep "ask first" on in the client.

revealed.title: Key created
revealed.warning: You will not be able to see this key again after closing. Copy it now.
revealed.notionNeedsPublicUrl: Notion needs a public address. Set one up first — see "How to get a public address" on the page. Copy the key before closing this window.
revealed.publicUrlUnverified: The last check of the public address did not pass. Notion may not be able to connect.

revoke.title: Revoke “{label}”?
revoke.desc: Agents using this key will lose access immediately. This cannot be undone.

rotate.title: Rotate “{label}”?
rotate.desc: Rotating issues a new key and the old one stops working right away. Clients configured with the old key (such as Notion) need the new key to keep working.

tools.title: Exposed tools
tools.helper: Tools external agents can see, grouped by the permission they need. Each key only sees the tools within its permissions; set write tools to "ask first" in the client.
tools.groupKeys: {count, plural, =0 {No active key has this permission} one {# active key has this permission} other {# active keys have this permission}}

advanced.title: Advanced
advanced.helper: Internal knobs + read-only paths; only touch if you know what you're doing

enabled.label: Outbox gradual rollout
enabled.helper: Sprint 15 reverse sync via outbox + FanoutWorker

host.label: SSE host
host.helper: Renderer hard-binds to 127.0.0.1; changing this breaks the connection

port.label: SSE port
port.helper: Renderer hard-binds to 9200; changing this breaks the connection

restart.confirmBody: The current sync batch will be interrupted (~5-10s downtime). Changed fields take effect after restart.
restart.statusProbeSlow: Service status probe timed out; verify from the status bar shortly
restart.pm2NotFoundHint: Run in Terminal: pm2 restart mail-sync

update.heading: Software updates
update.autoDownloadHint: Download new versions in the background automatically, then prompt to restart and install.
update.unsignedNotice: This is an ad-hoc signed build: update checks work, but new versions must be downloaded and installed manually from the releases page (in-app one-click update requires a signed build).

section.title: Custom folder sync
section.helper: Pick the folders to sync into MailAgent; their mail gets full AI triage, Notion sync, and full-text search. None selected by default.

pastDays.label: Initial sync window (days)
pastDays.helper: Only fetch the last N days; larger = slower first sync and more disk.

maxMessages.label: Per-folder cap (messages)
maxMessages.helper: Guards against huge mailboxes; truncates oldest beyond the cap.

picker.largeTip: Over 1,000 messages — first sync may be slow
picker.dirtyHint: Restart the sync service to apply
picker.orderOnlyHint: Display order only — applies immediately after saving

order.title: Synced folders
order.hint: Drag to reorder, click an icon to change it, set both switches per folder; the sidebar follows this order
order.grabbed: {label} grabbed at position {pos} of {count}. Use arrow keys to move, Space to drop, Escape to cancel.
order.cancelled: Reorder cancelled. {label} is back at its original position.

notify.head: Notify
notify.headTip: Notify: custom folders default to no push (FOLDER_NOTIFY_ENABLED is an allowlist)
notify.globalOff: The Feishu notification master switch is off — this column has no effect right now
notify.notApplicable: Built-in mailboxes ignore the per-folder switches: notification follows the global rules (priority + action type)

ai.head: AI
ai.headTip: AI triage: custom folders default to running it (FOLDER_LLM_DISABLED is a blocklist)
ai.globalOff: The AI triage master switch is off — this column has no effect right now
ai.notApplicable: Built-in mailboxes ignore the per-folder switches: AI triage is always on

pref.builtinHint: Fixed order, cannot be removed, icons not customisable; listed here so you can see where custom folders follow them
pref.builtinNote: The switches show a dash rather than off: both backend gates check for standard mailboxes first and skip them outright, so built-in rows are not governed by the per-folder switches. Icons are read-only for the same reason and never reach folder_pref.
pref.builtinLockTip: Built-in mailbox: fixed position, cannot be reordered or removed
pref.builtinIconTip: Built-in mailbox icons are not customisable
pref.archiveNote: Archive belongs in this section when it is on the list: STANDARD_MAILBOXES deliberately excludes it, so both per-folder gates apply to it literally and it gets real switches rather than a dash.
pref.defaultsHint: Icon and both switches take effect immediately — no sync-service restart needed. A newly added folder starts at notify off · AI on, matching the backend gate defaults.

motion.folder-clock: Minute hand sweeps a full turn
motion.folder-git: Node lights up, links draw outward
motion.folder-open: Front flap sweeps open along the outline
motion.folder-plus: Plus draws in two staggered strokes
motion.folder-root: Node lights up, root grows downward
motion.folder-sync: Cycle arrows turn half a round
motion.folder-tree: Trunk draws first, branches fade in
motion.folder-x: Cross draws in two staggered strokes
motion.folders: Front sheet slides out, the back one recedes

picker.emptyBody: No folders beyond Inbox / Outbox were found in your mailbox. Create one in Outlook, then hit Refresh.
picker.gatedBody: Folder discovery, selection, and sync are only available on the davmail backend. Switch backends under Accounts to enable this section.

manage.deleteRollback: The Exchange operation failed; the local folder tree was rolled back to the server's real state.
manage.deleteBodyWithCount: This deletes the folder on Exchange and the {count} synced message copies stored locally. This cannot be undone.
manage.deleteBody: This deletes the folder on Exchange and its synced message copies stored locally. This cannot be undone.
manage.deleteWarn: This folder may still be referenced by Outlook rules; deleting it breaks those rules. Already-archived Notion pages are unaffected.
manage.cleanupHint: Deletes only the {count} locally synced message copies — Exchange folder and emails are untouched
manage.cleanupHintNoCount: Deletes only locally synced message copies — Exchange folder and emails are untouched
manage.cleanupOk: Cleaned up local copies of "{name}" ({count} messages)
manage.cleanupFail: Failed to clean up local copies

matters.title: Matters
matters.description: Global settings for the Matters module. Per-matter follow-up rules and tags stay on the matter page.
matters.helper: Both apply to every matter — there is exactly one of each.

tags.label: Tag management
tags.helper: {total} tags, {count} currently in use; rename, recolor or delete them.
tags.loadFailed: Could not load tags — open the manager to retry.

agent.label: Follow-up agent
agent.helper: Built in, one instance: task contract, tool face and web-search tier.
